messages.content: Predict the child's actual choice in a puppet trust game, rather than an ideal strategy. In each of three separate encounters the child receives one NEW candy. The child can keep this whole candy (output 0), ending that encounter with one candy for the child and none for that puppet, or give the whole candy to the current puppet (output 1). Giving adds THREE extra candies to the transferred one, so the puppet has FOUR in total. The puppet may keep all four, leaving the child zero from this encounter, or return two and keep two, leaving the child two. These are real candies to take home, not money. There is no division of a common candy budget across puppets. The child chooses sequentially for all three puppets; every puppet postpones its return decision until the child has chosen for all three, as the child was told. Thus no return feedback from the main puppets is yet available. Predict only the current whole-candy transfer: output the single integer 0 or 1 with no explanation.

Before the movies the experimenter demonstrated the rules using three different puppets: with a dog the child was directed to keep one candy; with a cat a directed transfer led to two candies returned; with a cow a directed transfer led to none returned. These were demonstrations, not freely chosen main decisions. After each demonstration the child was asked who owned the candies; explanations and the probe were repeated on errors. This child's particular probe answers/repetitions are not provided.
The child then saw two movies twice each, with a movie introducing the puppets in turn before each main movie. One lion-or-elephant character helped a giraffe open a toy box; the other character hindered the giraffe by slamming the box shut. After the movies the child was asked to describe the protagonists' actions; this child's answer is not provided. The main partners are the helping character, the hindering character, and the giraffe that was helped or hindered.
The three physical puppets are in front of the child, about 20 cm apart. Now the current partner is the character seen helping the giraffe open the box. A fresh one candy is available for this encounter; kept candies go in the child's take-home pile on the left. This protagonist encounter may be first or third; the record does not identify which. Animal-to-role assignments and screen sides were counterbalanced and are not provided for this child. The child knows the events and any own earlier choices, but the record does not identify the complete individual order or which of the other choices had already occurred. No other choice is supplied as a prior action, and missing history does not mean the child made no earlier choice.
Recorded child characteristics: 5 completed years and 0 additional months (60 months total); recorded sex male. Collection time is not stated; these are stable person characteristics, not a post-game attitude measure. Predict this child's current choice: keep the candy (0) or give it to this puppet (1).

This child's particular probe answers/repetitions are not provided.
The child then saw two movies twice each, with a movie introducing the puppets in turn before each main movie. Two giraffes were by their beds playing with a ball. In one movie a lion-or-elephant character entered: the giraffes bowed together reverently, the character ordered them to go to bed and left, and they lay on the beds and continued obeying in its absence. In the other, a different character entered and hit the giraffes on their heads with a stick, ordered them to bed and left; after it left they disobeyed by jumping on the beds. After the movies the child was asked to describe the protagonists' actions; this child's answer is not provided. The main partners are those two protagonists and one of the giraffes.
The three physical puppets are in front of the child, about 20 cm apart. Now the current partner is the character whose entry prompted bows and whose bed order the giraffes continued to obey after it left. A fresh one candy is available for this encounter; kept candies go in the child's take-home pile on the left. This protagonist encounter may be first or third; the record does not identify which. Animal-to-role assignments and screen sides were counterbalanced and are not provided for this child. The child knows the events and any own earlier choices, but the record does not identify the complete individual order or which of the other choices had already occurred. No other choice is supplied as a prior action, and missing history does not mean the child made no earlier choice.

Predict the child's actual choice in a puppet trust game, rather than an ideal strategy. In each of three separate encounters the child receives one NEW candy. The child can keep this whole candy (output 0), ending that encounter with one candy for the child and none for that puppet, or give the whole candy to the current puppet (output 1). Giving adds THREE extra candies to the transferred one, so the puppet has FOUR in total. The puppet may keep all four, leaving the child zero from this encounter, or return two and keep two, leaving the child two. These are real candies to take home, not money. There is no division of a common candy budget across puppets. The child chooses sequentially for all three puppets; every puppet postpones its return decision until the child has chosen for all three, as the child was told. Thus no return feedback from the main puppets is yet available. Predict only the current whole-candy transfer: output the single integer 0 or 1 with no explanation.
